title: General Records, unissued sides and Lomax's use of Carew's copies
summary: Talk of unissued General Records items and Morton pieces Carew copied out for Lomax's book, including Naked Dance and Mamie's Blues; Morton's Washington sessions for Jazzman.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: The General Records The General Records
We're talking about those General Records and then... The General made, the General Records. Yeah. Well, there were some that were not issued, as you know. Yeah, those... Sporting House and...

Sporting House. I would like to have heard that Adam Mule dance, anyhow, whether it was worth putting on or not to know, because he played some very fine piano, as you know, from that one in the library.
Yeah, that's one that's never played much, you know. That's one of the better ones he did.
There's a score of that thing in Lomax's book.
Well, there's... No, I don't think.
Yeah, and Mr. Jethro. And Anamiel dance?
No, he's got Miserary. Miserary? He's got Miserary and Wine and Boy. I thought he had Mabie done. Miserary, Wine and Boy, Buddy Bowling's Blues, Naked Dance and Mamie's Blues.
Maybe I think about Naked Dance.

Yeah, Naked Dance. I made that for him, and I made the others too that I mentioned. Mamie's Blues, he asked if he could put part of it, he wanted to put part of Mamie's Blues in. I said yes, and sent him the copy of the music, and blessed he put the whole thing in. The others are excerpts that I copied myself from...
Well, you mean you sent him to Lomax?

Yeah, I sent him to Lomax. And he put him in. I have a manuscript of the Naked Dance, you know. I had to make it, yes. Wonderful extra chorus that he puts on there, at least in my estimation it is. Well that was for piano alone, not score. Just for piano. That's right. Yeah. Because he could do that with almost any piece of chorus, Johnny could. That's the remarkable thing about him. And as I say, when he was here in Washington and making those records that finally got put out by jazz man on the west coast, I went down there one night. Finger Buster and Honky Tonk and... Whining Boy and Creepy Feely. Yeah, those four. Those four were put out. But the night I was there, he made a fine recording, I thought, of that song, My Home is in a Southern Town. Mm-hmm.

Well, he made it for the same bunch, the boys that were taking it. They had him down there, and he thought they were going to issue him very soon, but of course they never did get issued until they got out to the Pacific. They never did carry them out there, and Dave Stewart and Ernie could put them out. Mm-hmm.
